research_updates.title: County records separate Apple equipment from Apple-associated real estate
research_updates.notes: The assessor names Apple Inc. on business-personal-property account 9372704 at 3740 S Signal Butte Road. The matching real parcel is owned by Platypus Development LLC, uses Apple's 1 Infinite Loop mailing address and includes a 1,255,156-square-foot Computer Center. The evidence view keeps both accounts separate. The parcel crosswalk supports site attribution but does not by itself prove current operating status.

source.title: Maricopa County Assessor — 3740 S Signal Butte Road parcel 304-33-005S
source.notes: The official parcel page identifies Platypus Development LLC as owner at 3740 S Signal Butte Road and gives its mailing address as 1 Infinite Loop, Cupertino. Improvements include a 1,255,156-square-foot Computer Center. The valuation table classifies the parcel as FOREIGN TRADE ZONES, legal class 6.2, with a 5% assessment ratio. This supports an Apple-associated site crosswalk but does not by itself prove current operating status. Tax year 2027 is displayed by the assessor but excluded because it is future to this review.

research_updates.title: Nine-year electricity series documents operating growth without converting use into cost
research_updates.notes: Apple reports Mesa electricity use rising from 45 million kWh in fiscal 2017 to 563 million kWh in fiscal 2025. The same report says Apple took operational control in October 2015, the converted data center began servicing customers in March 2017, and supporting renewable resources include the 50 MW Bonnybrooke solar project and 4.67 MW of onsite PV. Use is operator-reported rather than utility-meter verified; generation capacity is not load, annual output, avoided cost or capital spending.

source.title: Apple Environmental Progress Report 2026
source.notes: Apple reports fiscal-2025 Mesa electricity use, the supporting Bonnybrooke project's capacity, onsite PV capacity and operating dates. Electricity is operator-reported use; generating capacities are nameplate resources and not data-center load or output observations.

research_updates.title: Finaled permits document conversion, expansion and water-system work
research_updates.notes: Mesa permit rows identify Apple-era data halls, the Tilden AZ4 expansion, instrument-air, domestic-water, chilled/condenser-water, emergency makeup-water and soft-water-treatment scopes at parcel 30433005S. The application retains eight finaled or certificate-issued permit valuations individually. It excludes related addenda, Issued-only records and pre-Apple industrial work; no permit values are summed or treated as verified expenditures.

source.title: City of Mesa Building Permits dataset
source.notes: Official Socrata permit records were filtered to property_address 3740 S SIGNAL BUTTE RD and then to individually reviewed permit numbers. Retained rows have Finaled, C of O Issued or C of C Issued status. Total valuation is an administrative permit amount, not verified expenditure; related addenda, open Issued-only records and older pre-Apple industrial work are excluded. No permit values are summed.

research_updates.title: Current FTZ agreement links the premises to data-center and equipment activities
research_updates.notes: The Council-approved operator agreement identifies Apple Inc. and 3740 S Signal Butte Road and permits local data-center operations plus data-center-equipment assembly and high-tech manufacturing or storage of FTZ goods. It specifies a $1,000 activation fee and $5,000 annual administration fee, but the reviewed form has blank execution dates and no evidence of payment. No FTZ savings amount is inferred, and the agreement does not merge the separate real-property and business-personal-property accounts.

source.title: City of Mesa and Apple Inc. Foreign-Trade Zone Operator Agreement
source.notes: Council-approved ten-year operator agreement for FTZ 221 identifies Apple Inc., the 3740 S Signal Butte Road premises, permitted data-center and equipment activities, and municipal administration fees. The reviewed attachment is an agreement form without populated signature dates; no fee payment or FTZ tax-benefit amount is inferred.

research_updates.title: Water-treatment implementation is documented without a Mesa savings claim
research_updates.notes: Apple describes resin-treatment and sphagnum-moss work being implemented at Mesa, but its percentage reductions come from a pilot elsewhere and are not Mesa facility measurements. The study therefore adds no quantitative Mesa water-use or water-savings record. Permit descriptions establish system work, not consumption or avoided use.

source.title: Apple Environmental Progress Report 2025
source.notes: Apple's annual environmental report supplies the fiscal-2024 Mesa electricity-use observation and describes water-treatment work being implemented at Mesa without reporting Mesa-specific measured savings. It is an operator report.

economic_sources.title: Arizona Joint Legislative Income Tax Credit Review, 2024
economic_sources.publisher: Arizona Joint Legislative Budget Committee Staff
economic_sources.notes: The legislative review identifies Apple as the sole international operations center qualifying for the renewable-energy income-tax credit, estimates the confidential five-year credit cost from statute, and restates original Mesa investment and job promises from contemporaneous reporting. The review says available data cannot establish realization of those promises.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output.
